title: Specialty Pharmacy Program Enrollments: One Open Enrollment per Drug
content:
**Rule.** Under the Specialty Pharmacy Program a member may hold several specialty enrollments, one per specialty drug. There is no cap on the number of therapies a member may hold. A new referral for a drug may be opened only when the member has no enrollment for the same drug that is referred, in benefits verification, active or on hold.

## What the rule compares

- **The object.** The rule looks at enrollments of the *same member* for the *same drug*. An enrollment for a different drug never stands in the way of a referral, because each therapy has its own enrollment.
- **The evidence.** The member's enrollment records decide whether the condition is met. Each record shows the member, the therapy drug and the enrollment status, and those records are checked before the new referral is opened.
- **Distinguishing enrollments.** Each enrollment for a drug is a separate record with its own referral date.

## Status of an existing enrollment for the same drug

| Status of the member's existing enrollment for that drug | Does it prevent opening a new referral for the drug? |
|---|---|
| referred | Yes |
| benefits verification | Yes |
| active | Yes |
| on hold | Yes |
| discharged | No; this status is not one of the four listed above |

## Points of judgement

- *A member already holds an active enrollment for Dupixent and is referred for Skyrizi.* The Skyrizi referral concerns a different drug, so the Dupixent enrollment does not stand in its way.
- *A member's earlier Enbrel enrollment was discharged and the prescriber refers Enbrel again.* A discharged enrollment is not referred, in benefits verification, active or on hold, so it does not prevent the new referral.
- *A member's Humira enrollment is on hold.* A new Humira referral may not be opened while that enrollment is on hold.
- *How many therapies may a member hold?* There is no cap. The limit is one open enrollment per drug, not a number of drugs.
